resources.string: Describe it once; it runs on phone events
Results of scheduled tasks and automations
Failures, auto-pause and tasks waiting for you to unlock
Shown while automations wait for phone events
Each one opens filled in: check it, then tap Save. You can change anything first.
Start with a ready-made routine. It opens filled in, so you only need to tap Save.

Give me my morning brief. 1) Today\'s calendar events with times and places. 2) The weather where I am today: high and low, and rain or wind worth knowing about. 3) Notifications since last night that need action from me (messages from people, deliveries, bills, security alerts); skip promotions and routine app updates. Lead with anything urgent. Keep it under 12 lines.
Tells you when a price drops

Check the current price of %1$s at %2$s. Use the shop\'s own page and read the price for the item itself, not shipping or add-ons. If there is no previous result to compare with, reply with the current price, the currency and the link. If there is one, compare: when the price is now lower, reply starting with \"Price drop:\" and give the old price, the new price and the link. When it is the same or higher, or the price cannot be found, reply with exactly %3$s.
Atom checks once a day and tells you only when the price drops.
Item, for example a model of headphones
Where: a shop name or a link
Large files, unused apps and downloads, as a report

Make my weekly phone cleanup report. This is a report only: do not delete, move, uninstall or change anything, and do not offer to do it in this run. List: 1) The largest files on the phone (up to 10, with size and folder). 2) Apps I have not opened in the last 30 days, with how much space each uses. 3) What is in Downloads: how many files, their total size and the oldest ones. 4) Free storage left. End with a short list of what I could remove; I will decide and ask you myself.
Missed notifications and tomorrow\'s first event

Give me my evening wrap-up. 1) Notifications from today I may have missed, grouped by app, with the people who wrote to me first; skip promotions. 2) Tomorrow\'s first calendar event, with its time and place. Keep it short.
